source.note: Scan without a text layer. The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 10); PDF page n = printed page n. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.text_md: $2x^{2}-6x+1=0$  (correct to TWO decimal places)

Solve for $x$ and $y$ simultaneously:

$2x-y=2$

$xy=4$
Show that $2\cdot 5^{n}-5^{n+1}+5^{n+2}$ is even for all positive integer values of $n$.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for proving an exponential expression is even; tagged with exp.laws-of-exponents.

questions.text_md: Determine the values of $x$ and $y$ if: $\dfrac{3^{y+1}}{32}=\sqrt{96^{x}}$
questions.notes: Equating prime-power bases after writing both sides as powers of $2$ and $3$; tagged with exp.laws-of-exponents.

questions.stem_md: The first term of a geometric series is $14$ and the $6^{\text{th}}$ term is $448$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of the constant ratio, $r$.
Determine the number of consecutive terms that must be added to the first $6$ terms of the series in order to obtain a sum of $114\,674$.
If the first term of another series is $448$ and the $6^{\text{th}}$ term is $14$, calculate the sum to infinity of the new series.
If $\displaystyle\sum_{p=0}^{k}\left(\dfrac{1}{3}p+\dfrac{1}{6}\right)=20\dfrac{1}{6}$, determine the value of $k$.

questions.stem_md: It is given that the general term of a quadratic number pattern is $T_{n}=n^{2}+bn+9$ and the first term of the first differences is $7$.

questions.text_md: Show that $b=4$.
Determine the value of the $60^{\text{th}}$ term of this number pattern.
Determine the general term for the sequence of first differences of the quadratic number pattern. Write your answer in the form $T_{p}=mp+q$.
Which TWO consecutive terms in the quadratic number pattern have a first difference of $157$?

questions.stem_md: Sketched below is the graph of $h(x)=\dfrac{1}{x+p}+q$. The asymptotes of $h$ intersect at $(1\,;\,2)$.

questions.text_md: Write down the values of $p$ and $q$.
Calculate the coordinates of the $x$-intercept of $h$.
Write down the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of $g$ if $g(x)=h(x+3)$.
The equation of an axis of symmetry of $h$ is $y=x+t$. Determine the value of $t$.
Determine the values of $x$ for which $-2\leq\dfrac{1}{x-1}$.
questions.notes: Rational inequality, no dedicated skill; tagged with alg.quadratic-inequality (critical values and a sign diagram).

questions.stem_md:
The graphs of $f(x)=x^{2}-4x-5$ and $g(x)=a\cdot 2^{x}+q$ are sketched below.

- E and H are the $x$-intercepts of $f$.
- C is the $y$-intercept of $f$ and lies on the asymptote of $g$.
- The two graphs intersect at D, the turning point of $f$.

questions.text_md: Write down the $y$-coordinate of C.
Determine the coordinates of D.
Determine the values of $a$ and $q$.
Write down the range of $g$.
Determine the values of $k$ for which the value of $f(x)-k$ will always be positive.

questions.stem_md:
The graphs of $g(x)=2x+6$ and $g^{-1}$, the inverse of $g$, are shown in the diagram below.

- D and B are the $x$- and $y$-intercepts respectively of $g$.
- C is the $x$-intercept of $g^{-1}$.
- The graphs of $g$ and $g^{-1}$ intersect at A.

questions.text_md: Write down the $y$-coordinate of B.
Determine the equation of $g^{-1}$ in the form $g^{-1}(x)=mx+n$.
Determine the coordinates of A.
Calculate the length of AB.
Calculate the area of $\Delta$ABC.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for the area of a triangle from coordinates; tagged with ageo.distance-formula and fn.intercepts (vertices from intercepts and the intersection).

questions.text_md:
R12 000 was invested in a fund that paid interest at $m$% p.a., compounded quarterly. After $24$ months, the value of the investment was R13 459.

Determine the value of $m$.

On 31 January 2022, Tino deposited R1 000 in an account that paid interest at 7,5% p.a., compounded monthly. He continued depositing R1 000 on the last day of every month. He will make the last deposit on 31 December 2022.

Will Tino have sufficient funds in the account on 1 January 2023 to buy a computer that costs R13 000? Justify your answer by means of an appropriate calculation.

questions.stem_md: Thabo plans to buy a car that costs R250 000. He will pay a deposit of 15% and take out a loan for the balance. The interest on the loan is 13% p.a., compounded monthly.

questions.text_md: Calculate the value of the loan.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for a 1-mark percentage deposit (loan = 85% of the price); tagged with fin.present-value-annuity as the nearest loan-context skill.

questions.text_md: The first repayment will be made $6$ months after the loan has been granted. The loan will be repaid over a period of $6$ years after it has been granted. Calculate the MONTHLY instalment.
Determine $f'(x)$ from first principles if $f(x)=x^{2}+x$.
Determine $f'(x)$ if $f(x)=2x^{5}-3x^{4}+8x$.
The tangent to $g(x)=ax^{3}+3x^{2}+bx+c$ has a minimum gradient at the point $(-1\,;\,-7)$. For which values of $x$ will $g$ be concave up?
questions.notes: Uses that the gradient of the tangent has a minimum at $x=-1$, so the inflection of $g$ is at $x=-1$; tagged with calc.concavity.

questions.stem_md:
The graph of $y=f'(x)=mx^{2}+nx+k$ is drawn below.

The graph passes the points $\mathrm{P}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\,;\,0\right)$, $\mathrm{Q}(1\,;\,0)$ and $\mathrm{R}(0\,;\,1)$.

questions.text_md: Determine the values of $m$, $n$ and $k$.

questions.stem_md: If it is further given that $f(x)=-x^{3}+x^{2}+x+2$:

questions.text_md: Determine the coordinates of the turning points of $f$.
Draw the graph of $f$. Indicate on your graph the coordinates of the turning points and the intercepts with the axes.

questions.stem_md:
Points E and W are two variable points on $f'$ and are on the same horizontal line.

- $h$ is a tangent to $f'$ at E.
- $g$ is a tangent to $f'$ at W.
- $h$ and $g$ intersect at $\mathrm{D}(a\,;\,b)$.

questions.text_md: Write down the value of $a$.
Determine the value(s) of $b$ for which $h$ and $g$ will no longer be tangents to $f'$.
questions.notes: h and g are tangents at the ends of a horizontal chord of the parabola $f'$; they cease to be (two) tangents when $b$ is at or beyond the turning value of $f'$.

questions.text_md:
Given $f(x)=x^{2}$.

Determine the minimum distance between the point $(10\,;\,2)$ and a point on $f$.

questions.stem_md: A, B and C are three events. The probabilities of these events (or any combination of them) occurring is given in the Venn-diagram below.
If it is given that the probability that at least one of the events will occur is $0,893$, calculate the value of:

questions.text_md: $y$, the probability that none of the events will occur.
$x$, the probability that all three events will occur.
Determine the probability that at least two of the events will take place.
Are events B and C independent? Justify your answer.

questions.stem_md: A four-digit code is required to open a combination lock. The code must be even-numbered and may not contain the digits $0$ or $1$. Digits may not be repeated.

questions.text_md: How many possible 4-digit combinations are there to open the lock?
Calculate the probability that you will open the lock at the first attempt if it is given that the code is greater than $5\,000$ and the third digit is $2$.

figures.caption: Hyperbola $h(x)=\dfrac{1}{x+p}+q$ whose asymptotes intersect at $(1\,;\,2)$, with the vertical asymptote marked $1$ and the horizontal asymptote marked $2$.
figures.notes: p=-1 and q=2 (so $h(x)=1/(x-1)+2$) are derived from the printed intersection of the asymptotes and are asked in 4.1.1. Diagram not to scale.

figures.caption: Parabola $f(x)=x^{2}-4x-5$ with $x$-intercepts E and H, $y$-intercept C on the dashed horizontal asymptote of the exponential $g(x)=a\cdot 2^{x}+q$, intersecting at D, the turning point of $f$.
figures.notes: f is given, so E(-1 ; 0) and H(5 ; 0) follow at once. C(0 ; -5) is asked in 4.2.1; D(2 ; -9) in 4.2.2; a=-1 and q=-5 in 4.2.3. Diagram not to scale.

figures.caption: Straight line $g(x)=2x+6$ with $x$-intercept D and $y$-intercept B, and its inverse $g^{-1}$ with $x$-intercept C; the two graphs intersect at A.
figures.notes: g is given, so D(-3 ; 0) follows at once. The y-coordinate of B is asked in 5.1; the equation of g^{-1} (and hence C) in 5.2; A in 5.3. Diagram not to scale.

figures.caption: Parabola $y=f'(x)=mx^{2}+nx+k$ passing through $\mathrm{P}(-1/3\,;\,0)$, $\mathrm{Q}(1\,;\,0)$ and $\mathrm{R}(0\,;\,1)$.
figures.notes: m=-3, n=2, k=1 are derived from the three printed points and asked in 8.1; they match the later given $f(x)=-x^{3}+x^{2}+x+2$. Diagram not to scale.

figures.caption: Venn diagram of three events A, B and C, with given region probabilities $0,05$, $0,15$, $0,05$, $0,1$, $0,2$ and $0,183$, and unknowns $x$ (all three events) and $y$ (none of the events).
figures.notes: Printed decimal commas are kept as in the paper. x and y are asked in 10.1.1.
